record.paper_title: Problem collection from the IML programme: Graphs, Hypergraphs, and Computing
record.context_brief: Longest prescribed-endpoint path in a tournament
record.original_question: What is the computational complexity of finding a longest directed path from x to y in a tournament when x and y are specified vertices?

evidence.quote: Problem 10.4 (Conjecture 9.1). [3] What is the complexity of finding the longest (x, y)-path in a tournament?

artifact.self_contained_problem: A tournament is a directed graph $T=(V,E)$ obtained by orienting each edge of a complete undirected graph; equivalently, for every pair of distinct vertices $u,v\in V$ exactly one of the arcs $(u,v)$ or $(v,u)$ belongs to $E$. Given a tournament $T$ together with two specified vertices $x,y\in V$, an $(x,y)$-path is a directed simple path in $T$ that starts at $x$ and ends at $y$. Its length is the number of arcs it uses. Determine the computational complexity of the following problem: given as input a tournament $T$, two specified vertices $x,y$, and an integer $k$, decide whether $T$ contains an $(x,y)$-path of length at least $k$ (equivalently, determine the complexity of computing a longest $(x,y)$-path in a tournament). In particular, decide whether this problem is solvable in polynomial time or is NP-hard.
artifact.category_tag: complexity of path problems in tournaments
artifact.status_search_result: A brief web search did not surface a definitive resolution of the complexity of finding a longest directed path between two specified vertices in a tournament. Hamiltonian path in tournaments is well known to be polynomial, but the longest $(x,y)$-path variant with prescribed endpoints does not appear to have a publicly confirmed polynomial algorithm or NP-hardness proof in the sources retrieved.

status_evidence.title: Optimal Longest Paths by Dynamic Programming
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses longest path computations in directed graphs but does not resolve the tournament (x,y)-path complexity.
status_evidence.claim: No specific resolution of the longest (x,y)-path in tournaments problem is provided.

status_evidence.title: Finding Hamiltonian Path in Tournaments in O(n log n)
status_evidence.snippet: Every tournament has a Hamiltonian path, computable efficiently.
status_evidence.claim: Polynomial algorithms exist for Hamiltonian paths in tournaments, but the prescribed-endpoint longest path complexity is not addressed.
